messages.author: a259015b36a46546
messages.subject: Differential Time Trend - Type II Interaction
parts:
Hello,

I am assisting a colleague with their data analysis, specifically using a space-time interaction model. While working on this project, we encountered an issue with the estimates for the TYPE II interaction. We have noticed that these estimates change every time we re-run the same analysis. To illustrate this, I have attached two figures that display histograms of the values obtained from the same model run on two different occasions. The formula and models are below:

###formula
f1a <- age0_5 ~
  f(ID, model = "bym2",graph = g, scale.model = TRUE) +
  f(time, model = "iid") +
  f(Yr_id, model = "rw2") +
  f(ID.area.int,model="iid", group=ID.year.int,control.group=list(model="rw2")) # Type II Space-time interaction model - no spatial dependency but with temporal dependency

model1a <- inla(f1a, family="gaussian", data=DF_5,
                inla.mode='experimental',
                control.predictor=list(compute=T),  
                control.inla=list(strategy="adaptive", int.strategy="eb",reordering="amdc"),
                control.compute=list(openmp.strategy="huge", smtp="default", dic=TRUE, waic=TRUE),
                verbose=TRUE)
summary(model1a) #157
model1a$ok
########################################

Additionally, I have observed that the verbose output (also attached) contains several recurring errors. Specifically, we encounter the following error message:

*** PARDISO ERROR(0): not pos.def matrix: 1 eigenvalues are negative.
*** PARDISO ERROR: I will try to work around the problem...

It is worth noting that even when we attempt the analysis without using PARDISO, we still encounter a similar error.

Function: GMRFLib_factorise_sparse_matrix_TAUCS(), Line: 740, Thread: 5
Failed to factorize Q. I will try to fix it...

We would greatly appreciate your help in diagnosing and resolving this problem. He has consented to sharing the data with the INLA team, if this would help fix the problem.

messages.author: 66ed4f72a898a51c
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Differential Time Trend - Type II Interaction
parts:
Hi,

The precision matrix from the term
f(ID.area.int, model="iid", group = ID.year.int,
control.group=list(model="rw2"))
is _q I (x) R_, where I is the identity matrix with dimension equals
the number of max(ID.area.int) = n and R is the precision structure
matrix for the second order random walk which has dimension equals
max(ID.year.int) = k. Therefore the rank deficiency of this matrix is
2n. Since R has two eigenvalues equals zero, one related to an
eigenvector which is a constant and another which is proportional to a
linear function of 1:k. Because you have f(Yr_id, model = "rw2") in
the linear predictor, you need to add constraints in order to make the
model proper.

You can add it manually and use model = 'generic0' supplying the
constraints in the extraconstr argument. But a much easier and error
prune option is to exchange the definition by doing
f(ID.year.int,control, model="rw1", group=ID.area.int,
control.group=list(model="iid"))
where the needed constraints are already set.

best regards,
Elias
